summary: Backend-only 2nd retest of IPC 166A dead-law citation fix. PARTIAL PROGRESS: the single-turn 'IPC Section 166A' query now DOES return a citation chip with no flat-refusal prose (2 previously-failing tests now pass: test_ipc_166a_citation_chip_present_with_verbatim_text, and the LLM prose is a real answer, not 'I cannot confirm...'). However 2/6 tests still fail: (1) the dead-law/successor test fails because the surfaced successor text only names the Act ('Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023') without the specific section number '199' anywhere in the citation or prose; (2) the multi-turn follow-up 'what is the BNS equivalent?' STILL reproduces the original bug end-to-end (blank 'I cannot confirm this from the official text. Please consult an advocate.' with zero citations) because the new _has_explicit_dead_citation_with_successor exemption is recomputed per-turn from THIS turn's own retrieval hits matching the active ref's exact act+section — and the follow-up turn's fuzzy retrieval ('BNS equivalent') returns 3 different anchored BNS hits that do NOT literally match act=IPC/section=166A, so the exemption flag evaluates False on turn 2 and looks_like_refusal() suppresses all 3 citations again (confirmed in backend logs: 'citation_guard | suppressed | reason=refusal_text_detected | count=3'). Sanity checks pass: bare BNS 199 query correct, IPC Section 34 still a generic non-crash refusal. All 90 pre-existing unit tests (test_p0a/p0b/p0c/p1_grounding_fix) still green — no regression from the chat_router.py/answer_generator.py edits.

critical.endpoint: POST /api/chat/stream (message='what is the BNS equivalent?' as turn 2 after 'IPC Section 166A')
critical.issue: Multi-turn follow-up still fully reproduces the original bug (zero citations, flat 'cannot confirm, consult an advocate' refusal) even though turn 1 now works. RCA: _has_explicit_dead_citation_with_successor is recomputed fresh each turn by scanning THIS turn's own `retrieved`+`db_hits` for an entry whose act+section literally equals the carried-forward active_statute_ref (IPC/166A). Turn 2's retrieval text is a paraphrased 'BNS equivalent' query that returns 3 different anchored BNS hits (not an IPC 166A hit), so none of them satisfies `h_act==ref_act and h_sec==ref_sec`, the flag is False, and the unmodified looks_like_refusal() path suppresses all 3 citations when the LLM's own prose still reads as a refusal (backend log: 'citation_guard | suppressed | reason=refusal_text_detected | count=3').

minor.issue: Single-turn answer now shows a citation chip and the Act-level successor name ('Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023') via the LAW_STATUS_GUARD annotation, but never states the specific successor SECTION number ('BNS Section 199') anywhere in the citation payload or the LLM's prose — it says vaguely 'The successor law is found in the law.' This is a real gap vs. the task's expected behaviour ('WITH a dead-law/successor annotation pointing to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Section 199').

action_items: Fix the multi-turn case: the successor-aware exemption needs to be driven by the carried-forward active_statute_ref itself (IPC 166A, known from session/CaseState), NOT re-derived from whether this turn's OWN retrieval happens to re-surface an identical act+section hit. E.g., once a dead-citation-with-successor exemption has fired in a session for a given active_statute_ref, treat any immediate same-session follow-up that still concerns that same active_statute_ref as exempt too (or pass a lighter-weight 'is this turn a follow-up ABOUT the dead ref's successor' signal into the second guard), rather than requiring an exact re-match every single turn.

For the single-turn successor annotation, surface the specific successor SECTION number (BNS Section 199) in the citation payload / prompt instruction, not just the successor Act name — currently only the Act-level LAW_STATUS_GUARD line is shown.
No action needed: IPC Section 34 generic refusal (pre-existing data gap) and bare BNS 199 query are both confirmed still correct with no regression.
critical_code_review_comments: The exemption flag _has_explicit_dead_citation_with_successor is now computed and reused for BOTH guards (Layer M + citation_guard), which is a correct architectural pattern — but its underlying detection logic is still turn-scoped (re-derived from this turn's own retrieval), which is too brittle for a multi-turn conversation feature. Any follow-up phrased loosely enough to not re-trigger an exact act+section match in retrieval will regress back to the original bug. Recommend moving the exemption determination up to session/CaseState level (sticky for the rest of the thread once established) rather than recomputing from scratch per HTTP request.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Single-turn IPC 166A citation-chip bug is now fixed (confirmed via live HTTP test). Remaining work is scoped to exactly 2 items: (1) multi-turn follow-up exemption needs to be session-sticky, not re-derived every turn from exact retrieval re-match; (2) successor annotation should name the specific BNS section number (199), not just the Act name. Re-run /app/backend/tests/test_bugs_review_jan2026.py after the next fix — it already has correct assertions for both gaps (test_ipc_166a_has_dead_law_warning_and_successor and test_multiturn_ipc166a_then_bns_equivalent). NOTE for test running: EXPO_BACKEND_URL env var is not set in the shell by default (frontend/.env only has EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL) — must `export EXPO_BACKEND_URL=<that value>` before running pytest, as the test file reads os.environ.get('EXPO_BACKEND_URL').
rca_of_issue: Turn 1 (direct 'IPC Section 166A'): retrieval finds exactly one anchored db_hit whose act+section literally equals the active_statute_ref just extracted from this same turn's text, so _has_explicit_dead_citation_with_successor=True, both guards are exempted, and the citation now survives end-to-end — this part of the fix IS working. Turn 2 ('what is the BNS equivalent?', same session): the active_statute_ref is carried forward from turn 1's CaseState (still IPC/166A), but THIS turn's own retrieval (which runs on a paraphrased/translated retrieval_text, not the raw active ref) returns different BNS hits that do not themselves equal act=IPC/section=166A — so the per-turn re-scan in _explicit_exact_dead_citation_with_successor() finds no qualifying hit and the flag evaluates False for turn 2, even though the active_statute_ref variable itself is still IPC/166A. The fix's exemption condition conflates 'is a dead-with-successor ref active' with 'did THIS turn's retrieval also happen to find that dead hit again', and only the latter is actually checked.
